title: Lockheed Martin completes $3.4B acquisition of maritime defense company with Indiana presence
summary: Lockheed Martin completes 3.4 billion dollar acquisition of maritime defense company
detailed: FORT WAYNE, Ind. (Inside INdiana Business) - Global defense technology company Lockheed Martin now has its own presence in northeast Indiana after completing its $3.4 billion acquisition of Ultra Maritime, a manufacturer of advanced undersea warfare and anti-submarine warfare capabilities.

Headquartered in Braintree, Massachusetts, Ultra Maritime operates a manufacturing facility in Columbia City that produces sonobuoys, which are used to detect and identify objects moving in the water, particularly submarines.

Speaking at this week’s Northeast Indiana Defense Summit in Fort Wayne, Lockheed Martin Senior Vice President of Strategy, Technology and Business Development Mark Kenny told Inside INdiana Business Host Gerry Dick that the acquisition brings Ultra Maritime’s undersea expertise to the largest defense company in the world.
He said adding Ultra Maritime to its portfolio gives Lockheed Martin its first facility in Indiana.

(Inside INdiana Business) - Global defense technology company Lockheed Martin now has its own presence in northeast Indiana after completing its $3.4 billion acquisition of Ultra Maritime, a manufacturer of advanced undersea warfare and anti-submarine warfare capabilities.

ORIGINAL REPORT: Lockheed Martin completes $3.4B acquisition of maritime defense company with Indiana presence
Headquartered in Braintree, Massachusetts, Ultra Maritime operates a manufacturing facility in Columbia City that produces sonobuoys, which are used to detect and identify objects moving in the water, particularly submarines.

Speaking at this week’s Northeast Indiana Defense Summit in Fort Wayne, Lockheed Martin Senior Vice President of Strategy, Technology and Business Development Mark Kenny told Inside INdiana Business Host Gerry Dick that the acquisition brings Ultra Maritime’s undersea expertise to the largest defense company in the world.
“For northeast Indiana, it really brings some excitement, some adjacencies and some opportunities for the broad portfolio of Lockheed Martin,” Kenny said.
“We’re extremely excited about having the opportunity to be part of Lockheed Martin.

We’re staying the course on our production of sonobuoys here, but we’re looking at expanding into other markets, especially in the unmanned maritime side.”
The Columbia City facility was previously operated under the name ERAPSCO, which was a joint venture between Ultra Maritime and Illinois-based Sparton Corp.

That joint venture was dissolved in 2023, but Ultra Maritime continued to operate the facility under its own brand name
Kenny was a senior vice president at Ultra Maritime before the acquisition.
He said adding Ultra Maritime to its portfolio gives Lockheed Martin its first facility in Indiana.
“We are very proud of that,” he said.
“We love northeast Indiana, the patriots here, the hard work, the excellence, great for families.
We have a tremendous staff here.

They love the area, so we’re excited about the future.”
In addition to sonobuoys, Ultra Maritime produces sonar technologies, torpedo defense systems, radar solutions, electronic warfare and autonomous maritime sensing platforms.
The acquired business is now part of Lockheed Martin’s Rotary and Mission Systems business unit.

“Securing the undersea domain starts with giving sailors the tools and confidence to find, track, and deter threats that put ships and crews at risk,” Stephanie Hill, president of Rotary and Mission Systems at Lockheed Martin, said in written remarks.

“This is more than an acquisition – it’s a commitment to unite the best of our technology, capability and people to meet our partners’ urgent and growing demand for undersea warfare capability worldwide.”
Lockheed Martin did not specify if any jobs would be negatively affected by the acquisition.
